segments.text: Welcome to the daily Robotics news digest for September 19th, 2026.
Today we cover new supplier audits in China, a cool quadrotor build, and the latest ROS discourse.

From Humanoids Daily, Tesla reportedly begins new supplier audits for Optimus components in China, indicating a focus on manufacturing consistency and equipment commissioning as preparation for robot production.
Chinese media reported that Tesla initiated these new supplier audits for Optimus components in Ningbo on September seventeenth, with component orders already placed.
The audits focused on manufacturing consistency and equipment commissioning as preparation for robot production, employing a process designed to assess readiness for mass manufacturing.
Supplier representatives confirmed cooperation with Tesla on related robotics projects but did not explicitly confirm the latest audit visits.
These developments suggest progress in the supply chain alongside factory construction, representing a preparatory step toward realizing potential robot output.
This activity signals an intensified focus on establishing the necessary infrastructure for future humanoid robot deployment within the technology sector.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Two Birotors Make a Quadrotor".
This report details the development of an undulatory robot utilizing water for traction to successfully ascend inclines and clear steps.
NYU Tandon researchers engineered a system that employs water dynamics to generate the necessary force for climbing and overcoming obstacles.
The research involved designing a robot that interacts with the aquatic medium to achieve locomotion, demonstrating the viability of fluid-based propulsion for climbing applications.
Other related developments include the Kubi 2.0 desktop telepresence AI robot and an underwater quadruped robot featuring custom waterproof motor housings.
These advancements highlight progress in amphibious robotics and sophisticated AI agent engagement systems.
The ongoing research indicates further potential for novel locomotion methods in robotics and artificial intelligence systems.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: D-Robotics at ROSCon Global 2026 — Let’s Connect in Toronto"
reports on the presence of the D-Robotics team at the upcoming ROSCon Global 2026 event in Toronto.
The team will be connecting with the robotics community to showcase advancements in robotics development.
The D-Robotics group will exhibit an RDK X5 by Piper demonstration at the AgileX Robotics booth to illustrate on-device perception and artificial intelligence inference capabilities.

Furthermore, the team will engage with the LooperRobotics booth to discuss spatial artificial intelligence applications, leveraging the foundation of ROS 2 and the TogetheROS.Bot framework which incorporates hardware-accelerated capabilities.
This presence signals continued development in integrated on-device AI and spatial reasoning within the broader robotics ecosystem.
And that’s all the circuits we have for today, September 19th, 2026.
Keep those algorithms humming!
We’ll see you tomorrow for more robotic revelations.
Until then, happy coding!
